items.title: Fire safety managers, officers mandatory for 9,451 buildings from April 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: From April 1, 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings across the country designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint Fire Safety Managers (FSMs) and Fire Safety Officers (FSOs) at their premises. Fire and Rescue Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement was in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025, which requires owners of designated premises to establish a Fire Safety Organisation (OKK). "In future, the annual inspection reports prepared by FSMs will be assessed by the department for the renewal of Fire Certificates without requiring physical inspections to be conducted by the Fire and Rescue Department every year," he said.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia ends higher on positive regional sentiment
items.summary: Among the heavyweights, IHH Healthcare Bhd gained 15 sen to RM7.91, while Malayan Banking Bhd and CIMB Group Holdings Bhdeased three sen each to RM9.97 and RM7.70, Public Bank Bhd shed four sen to RM4.67, and Tenaga Nasional Bhd slipped 10 sen to RM12.90. In active trade, Zetrix AI Bhd and Supermax Corp Bhd improved 2.5 sen to nine sen and 46 sen, respectively, Top Glove Corp Bhd put on nine sen to 87.5 sen, V.S Industry Bhd inched up one sen to 33 sen, while ACE Market debutant SLGC Bhd slid three sen to 25 sen. Among the top gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd increased RM1.56 to RM44.96, Nestle (M) Bhd rose RM1.26 to RM91.26, Pentamaster Corp Bhd leapt 64 sen to RM6.08, Mi Technovation Bhd jumped 59 sen to RM6.00, and Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd improved 46 sen to RM21.32.

items.title: Fishmonger fined RM5,000 for peeping at neighbour in shower
items.summary: KUALA KRAI, Oct 6 — The Magistrate’s Court here today fined a fishmonger RM5,000 after he pleaded guilty to peeping at his neighbour’s wife last month. Magistrate Rais Imran Hamid also ordered Tuan Ahmad Farid Tuan Mat, 36, to serve nine months in prison if he fails to pay the fine. However, counsel Farazalila Fauzi from the National Legal Aid Foundation (YBGK), representing Tuan Ahmad Farid, pleaded for a minimum fine on the grounds that her client is single, earns about RM50 daily as a fishmonger, and supports his 66-year-old mother who has cancer.

items.title: Ringgit ends higher versus greenback ahead of 2027 Budget
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed marginally higher against the US dollar on Tuesday as investors kept a close watch on Budget 2027, to be tabled on Friday, for fresh trading cues, an analyst said. At 6pm, the ringgit climbed to 4.0835/0880 against the greenback from Monday's close of 4.0845/0890. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit is expected to trade within a narrow range ahead of the tabling of Budget 2027.

items.title: Countries weigh banning smart glasses over privacy concerns
items.summary: AUSTRALIA The federal government said in September it was considering barring the use of camera-equipped smart glasses in government workplaces due to privacy and security concerns. British cinema operators are also introducing policies to prohibit or restrict camera-enabled smart glasses, the UK Cinema Association said in August. Norway's capital Oslo banned smart glasses in schools in August.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM OCT 6, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ended higher today, in line with gains across major Asian markets following Wall Street's overnight technology-led rally. The benchmark index rose 1.60 points to close at 1,633.35 from Monday's close. In the crypto market, Bitcoin rose to RM350,869.

items.title: Tuaran MP calls for Sabah healthcare upgrade
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah's overcrowded hospitals and health clinics need urgent government action, a lawmaker said, calling for concrete and comprehensive measures to address the problem. Tuaran member of Parliament (MP) Datuk Seri Wilfred Madius Tangau said every recommendation in the Health Select Committee's report on its working visit to Sabah should be translated into clear action, funding, timelines and performance measures. "When health clinics lack sufficient space and staff, the pressure is transferred to hospitals.

items.title: Myanmar president to begin two-day official visit to Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing will undertake a two-day official visit to Malaysia beginning tomorrow. The Foreign Ministry said in a statement that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim would meet the Myanmar leader to discuss several key issues between the two countries. According to Wisma Putra, Myanmar is an integral part of Asean.

items.title: Ahead of Budget 2027, World Bank tells Putrajaya to raise revenue without raising rates
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Malaysia needs tax reform to address a structural decline in its tax revenue-to-gross domestic product (GDP) ratio, which has fallen to 12.7 per cent from 15 per cent 15 years ago, according to the World Bank lead economist Apurva Sanghi. “Federal government debt rose despite the contained deficit and now stands at 65.2 per cent. Yesterday, the Auditor General’s Report 2/2026 reported that federal government debt stood at RM1.32 trillion in 2025 compared with RM1.24 trillion in 2024, while the statutory debt stood at RM1.295 trillion, comprising Malaysian Government Securities, Malaysian Government Investment Issues and Malaysian Islamic Treasury Bills.

items.title: Friend struggles to accept death of student believed strangled by boyfriend
items.summary: KUANTAN: A polytechnic student is struggling to accept the sudden death of her close friend, remembering the 19-year-old as a soft-spoken and jovial person who was always there for their regular meals together. The diploma student, who declined to be named, said they had become batchmates at Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Polytechnic last year and shared many simple but memorable moments together. "We would usually meet up for meals together.

items.title: Fire at Johor Baru shopping complex triggers evacuation
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: "My legs were shaking" — that was how one worker described scrambling down the stairs after thick smoke from a burning car filled the basement of Johor Baru City Square shopping and office complex. Shoppers and workers were evacuated and directed to fire assembly points as firefighters tackled the blaze. The Johor Fire and Rescue Department said it received an emergency call at 3.40pm.

items.title: Top Glove's margins recover on tighter supply
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The demand-supply balance that occurred from the third quarter (Q3) onwards enabled Top Glove Corp Bhd to recover its margins for the financial year ended Aug 31, 2026 (FY26). Top Glove joint managing director Lim Jin Feng said there was an increase in average selling prices (ASPs) from Q3 mainly due to the increase in raw material prices, primarily nitrile and latex. Top Glove's earnings more than doubled in FY26 supported by growth in global demand.

items.title: Trump urges supporters to vote by mail despite fraud claims
items.summary: Speaking to reporters at the White House before departing for a rally in Nebraska on Monday afternoon, Trump said his supporters could vote by mail in the coming congressional midterm elections on Nov 3, even as he said he preferred in-person voting. "They can vote by mail if they want, because we seem to have no choice because a lot of people want to vote by mail, but a lot of very good people also want to vote in-person," Trump said. "Vote early, vote by mail or vote in-person on Election Day, November 3rd," Trump said.

items.title: Six Perak petrol stations inspected over alleged RON95 contamination
items.summary: IPOH: Six petrol stations in Ipoh, Taiping and Kuala Kangsar have been inspected following complaints that RON95 petrol was allegedly contaminated with water and had damaged consumers' vehicles. Perak Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry director Datuk Kamalludin Ismail said the inspections were carried out following public complaints and viral social media posts concerning the alleged contamination. "Preliminary checks using manual dipping methods and the Automatic Tank Gauge (ATG) system found no indication of water contamination in the fuel storage tanks inspected," he said in a statement.

items.title: Activists demand amnesty for protesters as Thailand marks 1976 massacre
items.summary: BANGKOK: Activists called for amnesty for people prosecuted under Thailand's strict royal insult law on Tuesday, during a ceremony marking 50 years since a massacre of demonstrators protesting dictatorship. A small group shouted "Amnesty 112" from a balcony at Bangkok's Thammasat University, an AFP reporter saw, as around 300 people including politicians and survivors gathered to commemorate the Oct 6, 1976, killings on the campus. The Thammasat crackdown 50 years ago followed the return from exile of military dictator Thanom Kittikachorn, who had been ousted three years earlier.

items.title: Why polls keep getting it wrong on Brazil's right
items.summary: "I am very pleased because many polling institutes had us trailing," right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro said after edging past President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in Sunday's election. The son of far-right former president Jair Bolsonaro, the opposition candidate secured nearly 47 per cent of the vote, compared to Lula's 45 per cent. The Datafolha pollster had Lula three percentage points ahead of his rival in the first round, while Quaest showed a one point lead for Lula.

items.title: Pay households, businesses to store power: Industry players
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Households and small businesses should be paid to store electricity and help ease pressure on Malaysia's power grid, industry players said. Suncrox Solar founder Noor Shahiwan said consumers who store excess electricity and reduce their reliance on the grid during peak periods should be compensated for the wider benefit they provide to the power system. Speaking at the 5th Solar Energy Storage Future Malaysia 2026, he said such incentives could encourage more consumers to install behind-the-meter energy storage.

items.title: Villa used as scam centre targeting Japanese
items.summary: Melaka Tengah district police chief Assistant Commissioner Halim Abas said the raid was conducted by the district police headquarters' Commercial Crime Investigation Division (CCID) following intelligence and surveillance. He said 17 foreign nationals, comprising 11 Japanese, four Chinese and two Myanmar nationals aged between 23 and 55, were arrested. Halim said police also seized 21 mobile phones of various brands, a laptop, two monitors, two central processing units (CPUs), two keyboards, two mice, a router, a notebook, 28 sheets of computer printouts believed to contain scripts in Japanese and two gate remote controls.

items.title: Dana Impak mobilises RM2.6bil for 130 firms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Khazanah Nasional Bhd's Dana Impak has mobilised RM2.6 billion in investments to support around 130 Malaysian and Malaysian-linked companies and more than 4,200 talent, according to the Dana Impak report. The report, launched on Tuesday, also sets out Dana Impak's catalytic role in crowding in capital and strategic partners alongside Khazanah. Jelawang Capital has supported five Malaysian fund managers under its Emerging Fund Managers' Programme and committed two fund managers under the Regional Fund Managers' Initiative.

items.title: Unhealthy air readings rise to 30 areas, Batu Pahat tops
items.summary: Johor had the most stations with unhealthy readings, at eight. Selangor and Pahang each had five stations in the unhealthy range. None recorded a very unhealthy reading.

items.title: RTS Link tackles gradient, wet-weather braking challenges
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A three per cent viaduct gradient and wet-weather braking are among the engineering challenges being tackled to ensure safe and reliable operations on the RTS Link. RTS Operations (RTSO) chief executive officer Dr Ahmad Marzuki Ariffin said the cross-border rail link might appear straightforward with only two stations, but its trains, tracks, signalling systems and infrastructure must work seamlessly to deliver a safe journey. Two stations.

items.title: 'It's okay, bro': Marshal took longer route to help George Russell cool down
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A race marshal who gave Formula One driver George Russell a lift back to the pits on his motorcycle took a longer route after seeing how disappointed the Mercedes driver was following his late retirement in Sunday's race. The marshal, identified only as Awang, said Russell was barely able to speak after he picked him up beside his stranded car. Awang said Russell's reaction prompted him to take a slightly longer route before returning him to the pits.

items.title: Mahfuz: Pas must resolve PN turmoil before seeking to lead Melaka
items.summary: MERLIMAU: Pas must prove it can provide clear leadership and unity within Perikatan Nasional (PN), said Amanah vice-president Datuk Mahfuz Omar. "When Pas took over PN's leadership from Bersatu, the question is whether PN became stronger or more fragmented," he said in a statement today. "RoS did not create PN's internal problems.

items.title: MediAsas basic medical insurance scheme to expand next year
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The government will expand the basic medical insurance scheme next year as part of reforms to tackle rising premiums and healthcare inflation, says Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin. Sim, who is also the Bayan Baru member of parliament, said he raised concerns over escalating medical insurance premiums and private hospital charges in parliament in 2024, prompting government action. "What is important is that the government has announced a basic medical insurance for Malaysians who can afford medical insurance but are now feeling burdened by the rising premiums," he said.

items.title: Chest a minute! Diner allegedly plucks out body hair and plants it in ‘char kway teow’ to dodge RM30 bill in Penang
items.summary: The alleged ruse was only discovered after the restaurant manager checked CCTV footage, which he said appeared to show the man repeatedly reaching inside his clothes before placing something into the dish. Cheng said the man later complained that he had found hair in the noodles. Suspicious, Cheng later reviewed the restaurant’s CCTV footage.

items.title: Socso cuts benefit claim processing time to 2.7 days from 5.3 days
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — The Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) has reduced the processing time for contributor benefit claims from an average of 5.3 days in 2024 to 2.7 days as of last year. He said the initial response time for complaint processing was also shortened from three days in 2024 to just one day in 2025. “Beginning 2025, the processing time for each benefit application under the Employment Injury Scheme, Self-Employment Social Security Scheme and Housewives’ Social Security Scheme has been reduced from an average of 5.3 days the previous year to 2.7 days in 2025,” he said.

items.title: MediAsas basic medical insurance scheme to expand next year
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The government will expand the basic medical insurance scheme next year as part of reforms to tackle rising premiums and healthcare inflation, says Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin. Sim, who is also the Bayan Baru member of parliament, said he raised concerns over escalating medical insurance premiums and private hospital charges in parliament in 2024, prompting government action. "What is important is that the government has announced a basic medical insurance for Malaysians who can afford medical insurance but are now feeling burdened by the rising premiums," he said.

items.title: Tunku Ismail meets MACC chief, newly appointed Johor director
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tunku Ismail, Regent of Johor, granted an audience to Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman at Istana Pasir Pelangi yesterday. Newly appointed Johor MACC director Datuk Hazrul Shazreen Abd Yazid was also present during the audience, according to a post on the official HRH Crown Prince of Johor Facebook page. During the audience, the MACC leadership reaffirmed the agency's commitment to strengthening anti-corruption enforcement and prevention efforts, as well as enhancing integrity and governance in Johor.

items.title: KLIA incident involving border agency chief: AGC to examine witness statements, evidence before deciding on further action
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) will examine witness statements, closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage and various other evidence before deciding on further action in connection with an incident involving Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain. Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said this after the AGC confirmed receiving the investigation papers on the case, which occurred at Terminal 1 of Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) on September 28. He said all evidence gathered during the investigation would be thoroughly examined to enable the AGC to determine the next course of action.

items.title: Monsoon transition phase to bring heavy rain, thunderstorms from Oct 9
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The monsoon transition phase is expected to begin on Oct 9 and continue until late October, marking the end of the Southwest Monsoon which began on May 14. Malaysian Meteorological Department (METMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said in a statement today that the country will experience weak winds blowing from various directions during this phase, creating conditions conducive to the formation of thunderstorm clouds. He added that with the end of the Southwest Monsoon, transboundary haze from neighbouring countries is expected to diminish gradually following changes in wind patterns.

items.title: Johor Regent receives MACC chief, new state director at Istana Pasir Pelangi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Regent of Johor Tunku Mahkota Ismail granted an audience to Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman at Istana Pasir Pelangi yesterday. According to a statement posted on His Royal Highness’ official Facebook page, the new Johor MACC director Datuk Hazrul Shazreen Abd Yazid, whose appointment took effect on October 1, was also present during the audience. “The meeting reflects the continuing working relationship between the MACC and the Johor Royal Institution in supporting the agenda of integrity and good governance,” the statement said.

items.title: Three crocodiles, including 4.75m giant, captured in Sarawak’s Batang Igan
items.summary: SIBU, Oct 6 — Three large-sized crocodiles measuring between 2.44 metres and 4.75 metres were captured within the last three days in Sungai Batang Igan near Ulu Kampung Kebuaw, Igan, near here. Jeferry said the operation in the area began on October 3, with three crocodiles captured so far. Two crocodiles measuring about 2.44 metres and 2.74 metres respectively were captured on October 4 and 5, before the largest, measuring 4.75 metres, was captured.

items.title: E-hailing driver tests positive for meth after crash kills 22-year-old Maldivian student near PJS toll
items.summary: The 37-year-old driver was carrying two Maldivian women when his Perodua Ativa collided with a Proton S70 near the PJS Toll Plaza at about 8.48pm on Sunday, according to Subang Jaya district police chief Assistant Commissioner Wan Azlan Wan Mamat. Police said the Ativa spun and overturned in the middle of the road following the impact. Wan Azlan said urine screening tests were carried out on both drivers following the crash.

items.title: Ex-German spy chief arrested for espionage, treason: Prosecutors
items.summary: BERLIN: Germany's former foreign spy chief was arrested Tuesday on suspicion of espionage, accused of seeking to pass sensitive information to overseas intelligence services, prosecutors said. August Hanning, who ran Germany's BND intelligence agency between 1998 and 2005, is suspected of charges including "attempted treason" and "espionage", according to a statement from federal prosecutors. Hanning's former chief of staff, partially named as Manfred D., was also arrested on suspicion of "aiding and abetting attempted treason and treasonous espionage."

items.title: Health Ministry mulls study on family breakdowns linked to doctors' postings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Health Ministry is considering a baseline study to determine whether long-distance postings are contributing to family breakdowns among medical officers. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the ministry currently lacked specific data on divorces or other family problems linked to medical officers being posted far from their spouses and children. He was responding to V. Ganabatirau (PH-Klang), who raised concerns over bullying, postings, transfers, welfare, and the brain drain among ministry medical officers.

items.title: Monsoon transition begins Oct 9, bringing thunderstorms, flash flood and fallen tree risks, MetMalaysia warns
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 6 — The monsoon transition phase is expected to begin on October 9 and continue until late October, marking the end of the South-west Monsoon, which began on May 14. Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said in a statement today that during this phase, the country will experience weak winds blowing from various directions, which are conducive to the formation of thunderstorm clouds. “These weather phenomena have the potential to cause flash floods, water surges, fallen trees, and damage to unstable structures,” he said.

items.title: ‘She should not wait any longer’: High Court rejects bid to delay RM1.48m condo prize for Miss Asia Malaysia 2023 winner
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Miss Asia Malaysia 2023 winner Luwe Xin Hui can proceed with enforcing a court order for a RM1.48 million condominium, or its cash equivalent, after the High Court rejected an attempt by the pageant organiser to put the ruling on hold pending an appeal. If the transfer could not be completed, the court ordered the company to pay Luwe RM1.48 million in cash instead. The court also ordered the company to pay RM5,000 in costs.

items.title: Thousands mass in France for high school protests
items.summary: PARIS: Thousands of demonstrators were massing under heavy police surveillance Tuesday in Paris and cities across France, as unions and teachers joined high school students who for days have been demanding better conditions in protests punctuated by violent clashes. Students have blocked the entrances to hundreds of high schools for 15- to 17-year-olds since late September, complaining of missing teachers, overloaded timetables, dilapidated classrooms and buildings that cannot cope with rising temperatures. In the Paris suburb of Creteil, where the protests started last month, students have piled barriers outside the Saint-Exupery high school.

items.title: High Court postpones Altantuya judicial review hearing to Jan 12
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court today postponed to Jan 12, 2027, the hearing of a judicial review application by the father of the late Altantuya Shaariibuu. The application seeks to compel police to investigate supplementary affidavits and a statutory declaration by former police officer Chief Inspector Azilah Hadri. In the application, Shaariibuu named the Inspector-General of Police, the Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director, the police , the Attorney-General, and the Malaysian government as respondents.

items.title: Foreign student attacked coursemate after break-up - Cops
items.summary: Sentul police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said investigations indicated that the suspect was unhappy with the woman after she ended their relationship. "The motive points to the suspect's dissatisfaction with the victim for ending their relationship," he said when contacted today. Anuar said the suspect, who was also a friend and coursemate of the female victim, was currently being treated at the psychiatric ward of Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL).

items.title: Nineteen-year-old motorcyclist killed in three-vehicle crash in Sepang
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 6 — A 19-year-old girl was killed after the motorcycle she was riding was involved in a collision with another motorcycle and a car on Jalan Sepang/Salak at about 8.20pm yesterday. Sepang police chief ACP Norhizam Bahaman said the victim, who was riding a blue Honda C100, was believed to have collided with a black Honda C100 motorcycle travelling from Sungai Pelek towards Nilai. “The black motorcycle is believed to have collided with the blue motorcycle, which at that time was travelling against the flow of traffic in the left lane of the same road.

items.title: Labuan water disruption enters third day, forcing eateries to halt operations
items.summary: LABUAN, Oct 6 — Thousands of consumers in more than 20 villages and residential areas across Labuan are grappling with a water supply disruption for the third consecutive day today, forcing several food and beverage operators to suspend business activities. Saadiah Said, 49, said the disruption had severely affected her business, leaving her with no choice but to temporarily close her eatery until the water supply was restored. Meanwhile, the Labuan Water Supply Department (JBAL), in its latest notice issued today, said repair works on the Phase Two Raw Water Pump (RWP) at the Lawa Gadong Water Treatment Plant in Beaufort, Sabah, were still ongoing.

items.title: Kedah MACC detains senior govt officer, two others over suspected RM155,000 graft in sports attire supply
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Oct 6 — The Kedah Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has detained three individuals, including a senior officer from a government agency, on suspicion of giving and receiving bribes amounting to approximately RM155,000. “The suspects, comprising two men and a woman aged in their 40s and 50s, were detained between 5pm and 9pm yesterday while present to give statements at the Kedah MACC office. Meanwhile, Kedah MACC director Datuk Nazli Rasyid Sulong confirmed the arrests when contacted and said the case is being investigated under Section 16(a)(B) of the MACC Act 2009.

items.title: Putrajaya autonomous EV bus service starts this week: Six stops, RM1 per ride
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Putrajaya’s Nadiputra public bus service will be joined by an autonomous electric bus starting tomorrow, October 7, 2026. ), the new self-driving EV bus service will serve Route P113, connecting MRT Putrajaya Sentral to Dataran Gemilang. — SoyaCincau pic The new Route P113 service runs a loop starting and ending at MRT Putrajaya Sentral, covering key administrative hubs along the way: MRT Putrajaya Sentral (Start) Kementerian Kewangan Istana Kehakiman Kementerian Belia & Sukan Dataran Gemilang Kompleks Perbadanan Putrajaya (PPJ) MRT Putrajaya Sentral (End) Currently, the operational hours of the autonomous EV bus appear to be rather limited.

items.title: Melaka International Cruise Terminal piling works reach 56pc, says CM
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 6 — Piling works for the Melaka International Cruise Terminal (MICT) project on Pulau Melaka here have reached 56 per cent completion, with 170 piles installed as of October 3. Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the remaining 134 piles are expected to be installed by mid-November, and the MICT project development comprises several key components, including an L-shaped jetty, a T-shaped jetty, and a Customs, Immigration, and Quarantine (CIQ) complex. Ab Rauf said the MICT development would open another international maritime gateway to Melaka, thereby paving the way for a greater number of international cruise ship arrivals and tourists to the state in the future.

items.title: Company director in Johor lorry chase case claims trial on attempted murder charge
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 6 — A 39-year-old company director linked to a 100km police chase involving a stolen lorry claimed trial in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of attempted murder. The accused, Chai Min Quan, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read out to him in Malay before Judge N. Kanageswari. According to the charge, Chai allegedly attempted to murder Noorulamin Soriani, 44, by ramming into him with a black Mitsubishi Triton at 8am on September 30.

items.title: PAS president Hadi Awang visits Dr Hasmah’s grave in Putrajaya, received by Mukhriz
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 6 — PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang visited the grave of Tun Dr Hasmah Mohd Ali in Putrajaya today, just over a week after the wife of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad died at the age of 100. Abdul Hadi shared photographs of the visit to the Pusara Negara in Precinct 20 in a Facebook post, where he also offered prayers for the late physician and public figure. Dr Hasmah’s son, Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir, was also at the cemetery and received Abdul Hadi during the visit.

items.title: Two men claim trial to Johor lorry theft after 100km police chase; one faces three more charges
items.summary: Chai Min Quan, 39, and Low Boon Lai, 37, pleaded not guilty after the lorry theft charge was read to them in Malay by a court interpreter before Magistrate A. Shaarmini. They were charged under Section 379A of the Penal Code for motor vehicle theft, which carries a prison term of between one and seven years and a fine upon conviction. Low was unrepresented.

items.title: Laos seizes 521kg of crystal meth from private jet arriving from Malaysia
items.summary: PHNOM PENH, Oct 6 — Lao police have seized 521 kilogrammes of crystal methamphetamine from a private jet reported to have arrived from Malaysia at Luang Prabang International Airport, with 13 people detained in connection with the case. According to the report, police later learned that the flight schedule had been changed, with the private aircraft due to arrive from Malaysia at Luang Prabang International Airport at 1.30pm on October 1. Officers subsequently found 23 suitcases and seized 500 packs of crystal methamphetamine weighing 521 kilogrammes, along with the Learjet private aircraft and a pickup truck as evidence, according to the report.

items.title: Exams board director: MPT4 aims to identify learning weaknesses before pupils reach secondary school
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 6 — The Year Four Learning Matrix (MPT4) gives schools a crucial two-year window to address learning gaps through targeted interventions before students enter secondary school. Examination Board (LP) director Abdul Aziz Mamat said the assessment was designed to help teachers identify and address students’ weaknesses as early as Year Five. He said the assessment data would enable schools to implement targeted interventions, such as strengthening teaching and learning (PdP) processes, providing remedial support to students who have yet to master basic skills, and offering enrichment activities for those who have already mastered them.

items.title: Nearly 9,500 buildings across Malaysia must appoint fire safety managers from April 2027, Bomba D-G says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — From April 1, 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings across the country designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint Fire Safety Managers (FSMs) and Fire Safety Officers (FSOs) at their premises. Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement was in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025, which requires owners of designated premises to establish a Fire Safety Organisation (OKK). “In future, the annual inspection reports prepared by FSMs will be assessed by JBPM for the renewal of Fire Certificates without requiring physical inspections to be conducted by the Fire and Rescue Department every year,” he said.

items.title: Immigration D-G says Myanmar repatriations will continue beyond initial 5,000
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 6 — The repatriation of Myanmar refugees will continue once the 5,000 individuals agreed upon by the Myanmar government have been sent home, said Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban. Speaking at a press conference on a special operation here today, Zakaria said 1,476 individuals were repatriated in the first phase last month, while more than 3,000 remain in the country. Based on UNHCR (United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees) records of issued cards, the number of registered refugees in the country now exceeds 200,000, with nearly half estimated to be Myanmar nationals, he said.

items.title: ECRL to deploy 200 auxiliary police after RM4m in cable theft losses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Some 200 auxiliary police personnel will be deployed at East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) hotspots from November as part of tighter security measures against cable theft and to ensure smooth rail operations. Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) chief executive officer Datuk Seri Darwis Abdul Razak said detection devices, alarm systems and closed-circuit television cameras had also been installed, while security guards and enforcement agencies were being engaged. Darwis said MRL, as the project and asset owner, remained confident that the ECRL could begin operations by mid-December 2026, based on positive results from System Integration Testing (SIT).

items.title: Jaya Grocer warns customers after Instagram account hacked, fake ‘Anniversary Promo’ posts push Telegram links
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Jaya Grocer has warned customers not to respond to fake promotional posts offering gold bars, iPhones and other prizes after its Instagram account was compromised. The supermarket chain said the posts, which purported to advertise an “Anniversary Promo” and directed users to a Telegram account, were not published by the company. Jaya Grocer said it was working to regain control of its Instagram account and would issue further updates once available.

items.title: Government to define Orang Asli advisory council powers in Act 134 amendments, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — The role and responsibilities of the Peninsular Malaysia Orang Asli Advisory Council will be finalised through amendments to the Aboriginal Peoples Act 1954 (Act 134), which will be tabled in Parliament soon. Deputy Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Rubiah Wang said the council currently operates as a committee that serves as an engagement platform between the government, the Orang Asli community, and relevant non-governmental organisations. On the socio-economic development of the Orang Asli community, Rubiah said the Department of Orang Asli Development (JAKOA) provides entrepreneur grants ranging from RM9,000 to RM35,000.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms and heavy rain in six states until 4pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Perlis, Kedah, Penang, Perak, Sarawak and Sabah until 4pm today. In a statement, MetMalaysia said the warning covered Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Yan, Kota Setar and Kuala Muda in Kedah, as well as Kerian in Perak, while the whole of Penang and Perlis were affected. In Sabah, the affected areas are Tambunan, Membakut, Keningau and Beaufort in the Interior; Ranau, Tuaran, Kota Kinabalu, Penampang, Papar and Kota Belud on the West Coast; Kalabakan, Tawau and Lahad Datu in Tawau; and Kota Marudu in Kudat.

items.title: Schoolgirl ‘taken away by man on motorcycle’ was hiding in toilet after row, Kulim police say
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — An alarming claim that an 11-year-old girl had left her school with a man on a motorcycle was fabricated by a fellow pupil after a dispute between the pair, police have said. Kulim district police chief Superintendent Syamsul Sinring said investigations found the girl had never left the school grounds and had instead hidden inside a toilet after an argument with a friend, Utusan Malaysia reported. Police were alerted after the school’s Senior Assistant for Student Affairs received information from two female pupils claiming the girl had left the premises with a man on a motorcycle.

items.title: Penang, MAHB ramp up plans for new international routes as PIA expansion progresses
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 6 — The Penang government will strengthen coordination with Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) to plan the expansion of international air connectivity in tandem with the ongoing expansion of Penang International Airport (PIA). He said the project would increase PIA’s annual passenger capacity from the current 6.8 million to 12 million, creating opportunities to introduce new international routes and increase flight frequencies on existing routes. Wong said the Penang government and MAHB would hold regular meetings on route development, aviation market trends and future projects involving PIA.

items.title: Malaysia to push stronger Asean action on transboundary haze next year, says minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Malaysia will harness its chairmanship and role as host of the 28th Sub-Regional Ministerial Steering Committee (MSC) meeting next year to strengthen Asean solidarity and shared responsibility in tackling transboundary haze. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the platform would provide an important avenue for strengthening regional cooperation to prevent a recurrence of haze incidents. Arthur said Malaysia had also tabled proposals on “Science Diplomacy” and a “Sustainable Haze Fund” at the 27th Sub-Regional MSC Meeting on Transboundary Haze Pollution in Bali, Indonesia, last July, with both proposals now under review by the Asean Secretariat.
